turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why does my son have a zero?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.
Then let's not waste it, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.
We're not on the same side, Hale. Owen has a zero, and you haven't answered me: who decided it, and when?
